full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J:- The Rule have been issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 05.07.2005 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Barisal, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 48 of 1994 reversing the judgment and order dated 13.07.1994 dismissing the Miscellaneous Case No. 79 of 1986 under Order IX rule 13 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex-parte preliminary decree dated 25.11.1958 and final decree dated 30.12.1977 of Title Suit No. 214 of 1957 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, (now Joint District Judge) 1st  Court, Barisal should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus that the defendant No.3 of Title Suit No. 214 of 1957 of the 1st Court of learned Subordinate Judge, Barisal filed a miscellaneous case under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 17.12.1980 for setting aside the exparte preliminary decree dated 25.11.1958 which was made final on 30.12.1977 contending inter alia, that no summons of the above partition suit was served upon him and the plaintiffs to the suit in collusion with the process server of the court managed to obtain a false service return and after fraudulent service of summons practicing fraud upon the court the plaintiffs obtained the preliminary decree behind the back of the defendant No.3 to the original suit. The defendant No.3 who is the petitioner of the miscellaneous case was in the dark about the existence of the suit which was filed against him and others. For the first time on 02.12.1986 the defendant-petitioner came to know about the decree from one Sirajul Hoque Sharif. Thereafter, the defendant no.3 being petitioner preferred the miscellaneous case for setting aside the exparte decree obtained against him fraudulently. 

 3. The contrary case of the plaintiff-opposite party No.I 9 of the case in brief is such that the summons was duly served upon the petitioner, who was the defendant no.3 to the original partition suit and the petitioner is in no way prejudiced by the impugned judgment and decree but only to harass the plaintiff he filed the miscellaneous case on false allegation. 

 4. The learned trial court i.e. the 1st court of Subordinate Judge, Barisal by his judgment and order dated 13.07.1994 dismissed the miscellaneous case and being aggrieved the defendant-petitioner preferred a miscellaneous appeal in the court of learned District Judge, Barisal being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 48 of 1994 which was heard and disposed of by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Barisal and the learned appellate court below by the impugned judgment and order dated 05.07.2005 allowed the miscellaneous appeal reversing the judgment and order passed by the learned trial court and set aside the exparte preliminary decree dated 25.11.1958. 

 7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the appellate court below during disposal of the miscellaneous appeal committed illegality and irregularity in holding that the summons of the original suit was suppressed upon the defendant-petitioner and the defendant-petitioner was in the dark about the existence of the partition suit filed against him and others. The learned Advocate further submits that under the provisions of section 114(e) of the Evidence Act, 1872 it has got a presumptive value that the process server of the court duly served the summons notice upon the defendant-petitioner and nothing has been suppressed. In allowing the appeal the learned lawyer appellate court committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate also submits that the miscellaneous case under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was hopelessly time barred and the petitioner to the case was not in a position to prove his date of knowledge as alleged in the contents of the application. The only witness of the petitioner not corroborated the petitioner during his deposition before the trial court and the learned lower appellate court misconstrued the decision reported in 35 DLR(AD)162. 

 8. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule controverted the grounds mentioned by the learned counsel for the petitioner and submits that in the original partition suit the petitioner of the miscellaneous case was the defendant no.3 and he was quite in the dark about the existence of the suit which was filed against him. The service of summons is collusive, fraudulent and it was suppressed by the concerned process-server of the court in collusion with the plaintiff to the suit and practicing fraud upon the court the plaintiff-opposite party obtained the preliminary decree which was exparte against the defendant-petitioner. The learned Advocate further submits that because of the suppression of summons the date of knowledge of the defendant-petitioner is immaterial and the learned lower appellate court was quite justified in relying upon the decision of our Apex Court reported in 35 DLR(AD)162. The learned Advocate further submits that the allegation which was set-forth by the defendant-petitioner in his miscellaneous case was not challenged by the plaintiff-opposite party during hearing of the miscellaneous case. The defendant-petitioner was not even cross-examined from the side of the plaintiff to controvert or falsify the specific assertion of the defendant no.3 of the original suit. As such the testimony of the defendant-petitioner remained unchallenged, which amounts to admission from the side of the plaintiff. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the appellate court below after proper assessment of evidence and appreciation of law rightly decided the merit of the appeal in favour of the defendant-appellant and there is nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Barisal. 

 9. Heard the learned Advocates of both sides, perused the impugned judgment and order along with the judgment and order passed by the trial court in Miscellaneous Case being No. 79 of 1986 under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the judgment and decree passed on 15.11.1958, which was finally disposed of in the form of final decree on 30.12.1977. 

 10. On perusal of the connected papers, it transpires that the petitioner to the miscellaneous case was the defendant no.3 to the original' suit which was disposed of against him exparte. It is the clear contention of the defendant-petitioner that he was not in the know about the existence of the suit filed against him and the summons notice was suppressed fraudulently by the process-server of the court in collusion with the plaintiff to the suit. By practicing fraud upon the court the decree was obtained exparte against the defendant-petitioner and the defendant-petitioner knowing about the decree passed against him for the first time on 02.12.1986 preferred the miscellaneous case for setting aside the judgment and decree passed against him. 

 11. On careful scrutiny over the papers it is apparent that the learned trial court during disposal of the miscellaneous case examined two witnesses from the side of the defendant-petitioner therein and no witness was produced from the side of the plaintiff-opposite parties. It appears from the records that the defendant-petitioner, who was examined as witness No.1 was not cross-examined from the side of the plaintiff-opposite party. It was asserted by the defendant-petitioner in his deposition that he was not in the know about the suit filed against him and he did not receive any summons of the Court. The process-server of the court did not serve any summons notice upon him as alleged and the service return as it appears is collusive and fraudulent. The learned trial court at the time of disposal of the miscellaneous case is misconceived in holding the basic criterion of the case under order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The pertinent question is as to whether the service of summons was properly done or not. Apparently; the trial court without going into the merit of the service return banked upon the deposition of the witness No.2 for the petitioner from whom the petitioner for the first time allegedly came to know about the exparte decree. 

 12. We have come across from the connected documents that the contention of the petitioner as stated by him in his examination-in-chief was not contradicted or challenged from the side of the plaintiff-opposite party. The plaintiff-opposite party remained silent despite he filed the written objection initially against the pleading of the defendant-petitioner. In this context this Bench decided in a case law reported in 18 BLC 386 in the case of Shamir Chandra Sawjal and others —vs.- Government of Bangladesh that the failure of cross-examine the plaintiff's witness to falsify the case of the plaintiff or controvert the positive assertion of the witness as appears from his examination-in-chief tantamounts to admission from the side of the defendant. In giving the aforesaid decision this Bench relied upon the decision of our Apex Court in the case of Abdur Rashid —vs.- Alz.al Kazi reported in 16 MLR(AD)4. 

 13. Furthermore, once when the defendant denies the service of summons upon him; the whole onus shifts to the plaintiff to prove that in-fact summons was duly served and that is the decision of our Appellate Division in several case laws reported in 16 BLD(AD)4, 1 BLC(AD)179 and when the Court is satisfied that there was no due service of summons, it is bound to set aside the ex-perte decree and in that case knowledge is immaterial (Ref. 35 DLR (AD)162; 4 BLD (AD) 83; 1983 BCR (AD) 207 and 12 BLC (AD) 75). 

 15. Having regard to the facts, circumstances and discussions made above, I am constrained to hold such a view that the learned lower appellate court was quite justified in allowing the miscellaneous appeal and rightly reversed the judgment and order passed by the trial court. 

 16. In the result, the Rule having no merit is discharged without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and order dated 05.07.2005 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Barisal, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 48 of 1994 reversing the judgment and order dated 13:07.1994 dismissing the Miscellaneous Case No. 79 of 1986 under Order IX rule 13 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex-parte preliminary decree dated 25.11.1958 and final decree dated 30.12.1977 of Title Suit No. 214 of 1957 is hereby affirmed.
